extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the Ford Foundation Predoctoral Fellowship (Ph.D./Sc.D.) program
extracted.subtask_description: Applying for the Ford Foundation Predoctoral Fellowship: meeting eligibility requirements, preparing required application and supplementary materials, and addressing the program's selection factors emphasizing diversity and academic promise. Includes strict deadlines and documentation rules for a national competition administered by the National Academies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase the diversity of the nation’s college and university faculties by increasing their ethnic and racial diversity; maximize the educational benefits of diversity; increase the number of professors who can and will use diversity as a resource for enriching the education of all students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These goals frame selection priorities and applicant statements should demonstrate alignment with these aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core selection judgment (review panel standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards will be made to individuals who, in the judgment of the review panels, have demonstrated superior academic achievement, are committed to a career in teaching and research at the college or university level, show promise of future achievement as scholars and teachers, and are well prepared to use diversity as a resource for enriching the education of all students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels use academic records, essays, letters of recommendation, the application itself, and other appropriate materials as the basis for this judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive factor: Evidence of superior academic achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of superior academic achievement (such as grade point average, class rank, honors, or other designations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide transcripts and other documentation of academic honors; this is both an eligibility element and a selection positive factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive factor: Degree of promise as scholars and teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of promise of continuing achievement as scholars and teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essays, research statements, and letters of recommendation should speak to future scholarly and pedagogical potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive factor: Capacity to respond pedagogically to diverse students
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to respond in pedagogically productive ways to the learning needs of students from diverse backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal statements should describe concrete pedagogical strategies or experiences demonstrating this capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive factor: Sustained engagement with underrepresented communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustained personal engagement with communities that are underrepresented in the academy and an ability to bring this asset to learning, teaching, and scholarship at the college and university level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence and examples of engagement, and explain how this experience will inform teaching and scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive factor: Likelihood of using diversity as an educational resource
rubrics_metrics.description: Likelihood of using the diversity of human experience as an educational resource in teaching and scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss specific plans or past instances illustrating how diversity will be used pedagogically or in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive factor: Membership in specified underrepresented groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership in one or more of the following groups whose underrepresentation in the American professoriate has been severe and longstanding: Alaska Natives; Black/African Americans; Mexican Americans/Chicanas/Chicanos; Native American Indians; Native Pacific Islanders; Puerto Ricans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-identification is a positive factor; applicants who belong to these groups should indicate this in the application where requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Citizenship and immigration status
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants include all U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and U.S. permanent residents (holders of a Permanent Resident Card); individuals granted deferred action status under DACA; Indigenous individuals exercising rights associated with the Jay Treaty; individuals granted Temporary Protected Status; political asylees; and refugees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be able to provide satisfactory documentation of status if awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Commitment to academic career
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals must be committed to a career in teaching and research at the college and university level in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal statement and career goals should clearly articulate this commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Enrollment in or plan to enroll in an eligible research-based Ph.D./Sc.D. program
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be enrolled in or planning to enroll in an eligible research-based (dissertation-required) program leading to a Ph.D. or Sc.D. at a non-proprietary (not for profit) U.S. institution of higher education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field of study must be one of the eligible fields listed; institution must be fully accredited and non-profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Minimum of three years remaining to complete degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who as of the 2021 fall semester require a minimum of three years of study to complete their Ph.D. or Sc.D. degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants already in doctoral programs must provide a Verification of Doctoral Degree Status signed by the graduate adviser or department chair confirming at least three years remaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: No prior doctoral degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who have not earned a doctoral degree at any time, in any field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt of the fellowship is conditioned upon awardees providing satisfactory documentation that they meet all eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible fields of study
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards will be made for study in research-based Ph.D. or Sc.D. programs in fields including (but not limited to) American studies, anthropology, archaeology, art and theater history, astronomy, chemistry, communications, computer science, cultural studies, earth sciences, economics, engineering, ethnic studies, ethnomusicology, geography, history, international relations, language, life sciences, linguistics, literature, mathematics, performance study, philosophy, physics, political science, psychology, religious studies, sociology, urban planning, women’s studies, interdisciplinary ethnic studies, area studies, peace studies, and social justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research-based fields of education are eligible only if the major field of study is one of the listed fields and described as the applicant's Ph.D./Sc.D. program (e.g., sociology of education).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible programs, degrees, and joint-degree restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals enrolled in programs such as administration, audiology, business, consumer studies, curriculum development, exercise physiology, filmmaking, fine arts, guidance, human resource management, kinesiology, leadership, library and information science, management, nursing, occupational health, performing arts, personnel, physical education, physical therapy, public health, rehabilitation science, social welfare, social work, speech pathology, and teacher education will not be supported unless the program is research-based and dissertation-required. Awards will not be made for work leading to terminal master’s degrees, the Ed.D., D.F.A., Psy.D., professional degrees (medicine, law, public health), or for study in joint-degree programs (M.D./Ph.D., J.D./Ph.D., M.F.A./Ph.D.). This program does not support the Ph.D. portion of a dual-degree program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must document that their program is dissertation-required and research-based when applying from potentially ineligible program areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship institution eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are tenable at any fully accredited, non-proprietary (not for profit) U.S. institution of higher education offering a Ph.D. or Sc.D. degree in an eligible field of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should confirm their institution meets these criteria before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous graduate study and applicant statuses accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended for applicants who are undergraduates in their senior year, individuals who have completed undergraduate study, individuals who have completed some graduate study, and individuals already enrolled in a Ph.D. or Sc.D. program who provide evidence that they can fully utilize a three-year fellowship award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If already in a doctoral program, a Verification of Doctoral Degree Status form signed by the graduate adviser or department chair is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend and fellowship benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual stipend of $27,000 for three years; an invitation to attend the Conference of Ford Fellows; access to Ford Fellow Regional Liaisons and other networking resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional supplementation is encouraged; fellowship tenure includes participation in program activities and networking opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenure rules and deferral policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows must begin the first year of tenure on September 1, 2021. After the first year they may defer funding for one or two years but must use all three years of support within the five-year period of eligibility. During Ford Fellowship tenure years, Fellows must remain on tenure full-time for the academic year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting the award affirms intention to use a total of three years of Ford predoctoral fellowship support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of fellowship (restrictions during tenure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predoctoral Fellows are required to enroll full-time in a dissertation-required program and may not accept full-time teaching or research appointments, other major fellowships, internships, or similar internal or external awards during fellowship tenure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows must agree to Terms of Appointment, participate in Directory updates and periodic surveys designed to demonstrate the program's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines and strict enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Online application must be submitted by December 17, 2020, 5:00 PM EST. Supplementary materials must be uploaded by January 7, 2021, 5:00 PM EST. No extensions or exceptions will be made for these deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items listed in bold are required by the application deadline; incomplete applications will not be included in the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online application required elements (initial submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information, demographic information, education history (name, location, enrolled dates, degree received or currently pursuing, and research field for all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended or currently attending as of fall 2020), employment history, honors, and awards; personal statement addressing specified prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All application materials must be written in English and become the property of the National Academies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal statement content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal statement must describe the applicant’s background, experience, and commitment to the goals of the Ford Foundation Fellowship Programs by addressing applicable items: capacity to respond pedagogically to diverse students; sustained engagement with underrepresented communities and ability to bring that asset to academia; likelihood of using diversity as an educational resource; membership in specified underrepresented groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address all that apply; be specific and provide examples/evidence linking experience to program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials required (to be uploaded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Baccalaureate transcripts showing all undergraduate coursework completed prior to fall 2020; graduate transcripts if enrolled in graduate program (or unofficial grade report if no transcript yet for program started in fall 2020); Verification of Doctoral Degree Status form for applicants in doctoral programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unofficial transcripts or grade reports are acceptable for review; official transcripts will be required if offered a fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of scholarly productivity and proposed plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of previous research and scholarly productivity including a list of publications and presentations; proposed plan of graduate study and research and the applicant’s long-range career goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, concrete descriptions of past productivity and a feasible, coherent plan for graduate study and career trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of recommendation: three minimum; five maximum. Applications with fewer than three letters submitted by January 7, 2021, at 5 PM EST will not be reviewed. If currently in graduate school, at least one letter should be submitted by a faculty adviser or other faculty member in the applicant’s current department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting four or five letters is recommended to ensure the minimum number is received; use online notification tool to send referees the upload link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness monitoring and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should regularly monitor application completeness using tools provided; ensure all required supplementary materials have been received before the January 7, 2021 deadline. Incomplete applications will not be included in the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extensions or exceptions will be made; proactively follow up with letter writers and institutions for transcripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance preparation and file formatting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare essays in advance and save each in a separate PDF file (maximum 4 MB); get feedback from advisers, mentors, and colleagues; review essays for typos and grammatical errors; contact potential letter writers and provide them with a draft of your research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be certain letter writers agree to upload letters by the Jan 7 deadline; enter their names/emails into the online system and use the notification tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award obligations and program participation
rubrics_metrics.description: By accepting the award, Fellows must agree to the Terms of Appointment, participate in periodic Directory updates and surveys designed to demonstrate the program’s impact, and attend the Conference of Ford Fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in program activities (conference, mentoring network) and responding to surveys are conditions accompanying the award.
